title: From Free to Leads: The Power of Email
overview: Vishen made the case that email, not social media, is the asset your business is built on, and showed you exactly how he learned that in 2003 when a nine-lesson email sequence lifted his first website's sales 94% overnight. You left with the three rules of a great autoresponder, a modern seven-step email sequence to copy, four subject-line formulas and a simple way to use AI to write your sequence from your own course material.
key_ideas: Social media builds reach, email builds relationships, and relationships build revenue. Mindvalley still makes more than ten times the revenue from email that it makes from social media. Email is not sexy, but email is money.

The one number every expert should obsess over is the size of your email list, because it is the one asset the algorithm cannot take away. When Facebook changed its algorithm in 2010, pages with a million followers dropped from reaching 100,000 people to 5,000 and businesses collapsed; Mindvalley's did not, because it had email. Your list is your business's immune system: in a WhatsApp group of over 100 Mindvalley authors, someone loses an Instagram or TikTok account every few months, but nobody loses their email list. Nora at Alba Health builds hers two ways, a free assessment quiz and a newsletter sign-up; start with the newsletter because it is easier.

Vishen's 2003 origin story: he built a Silva Method website, lost money for three months, then read a 65-page book by a Malaysian marketer with one idea: create an email autoresponder that gives away free information drip style. He spent 30 days writing nine lessons (Living Your Alpha Life). Overnight, sales rose 94%, and doubled conversions meant ads became profitable, affiliates wanted to mail for him and everything compounded. Over a million people eventually signed up.

Rule 1, put your best foot forward first: do not give away your weakest content. He gave away the single thing that blows every Silva student away, the 22-minute Silva Centering Exercise, as a free MP3 in Lesson 2 and did not care if it was pirated.

Rule 2, educate the user: build the case for why your product matters. In 2003 meditation was fringe, so he explained beta, alpha, theta and delta brainwaves, told the story of Thomas Edison's naps, and backed creative visualisation with quotes from the Washington Times and CBS News. Everywhere, add science and data.

Rule 3, drip feed: do not give everything at once. Picture Cleopatra being fed grapes one at a time. Lessons went out with reminder emails in between (did you get Lesson 1? here is 20% off the course), roughly every 48 hours, so that by Lesson 9 people were desperate to buy.

You do not need to be the author or own the product; you need to understand the system. Vishen was only an affiliate for a publisher's Silva course but out-sold their own website, built a 200,000-person list, and used it to go directly to Jose Silva's family and create his own programme.

After the autoresponder, do not stop. Non-buyers move into a daily newsletter (Mindvalley Daily goes out five times a week) after 14 days, where they may discover a different teacher. Buyers move into a customer nurturing sequence. Segment everyone by tagging: lead magnet, quiz taken, masterclass watched, emails opened, links clicked, purchases made.

frameworks.name: The Three Rules of the Autoresponder Sequence
steps: Put your best foot forward first: give away your best content free, not your weakest.
Educate the user: explain why your product matters, with science, data and stories.
Drip feed: release one lesson at a time, roughly every 48 hours, with reminder emails in between.

frameworks.name: The Email Flow After Sign-Up
steps: Lead magnet list: they sign up to solve one thing (PDF, white paper, webinar) and you deliver value fast.
Autoresponder sequence: drip the lessons over about 14 days.
Buyers go into a customer nurturing sequence; non-buyers go into your daily or regular newsletter for the ongoing relationship.

frameworks.name: Four Sticky Subject Line Ideas
steps: Ask a question: Are you making this mistake?
Make a bold claim: I was wrong about meditation.
Use a number: Three things I wish I'd known at 30 (odd numbers tested better).
Create curiosity: What happened when I stopped checking email?

exercises: Screenshot the seven-step email sequence (deliver the lead magnet, origin story, core belief, quick win, social proof, introduce your offer, direct invite). Paste it into Claude along with your course transcript and ask it to create an email autoresponder sequence in that format, dripping the content, leading with your best lesson, and educating readers who do not yet understand your product with science and data.
Visit AlbaHealth.com and sign up for the newsletter and the free assessment to experience a student's working example of the two email capture methods.
Screenshot the four subject-line formulas and rewrite your next three subject lines using them.
next_steps: Identify your single best lesson or exercise and make it the free lead magnet, delivered in the first or second email.
Draft or generate your seven-email autoresponder this week and set it to send roughly every 48 hours.
Add a newsletter sign-up to your website first (quizzes can come later) and choose the regular cadence you will actually keep.
Set up basic tags in your email tool so buyers and non-buyers receive different sequences.
